{{Short description|French mathematician}}
[[Image:Antoine Deparcieux (1703-1768).jpg|thumb|Antoine Deparcieux]]
'''Antoine Deparcieux''' (28 October 1703{{snd}}2 September 1768) was a French [[mathematician]].
He was born at [[Clessous]] in the [[Portes, Gard|Portes]], province of [[Languedoc]]. He attended the school of [[Saint-Florent-sur-Auzonnet|Saint Florent]] for 10 years while working on his family farm. In 1725, his desire for learning took him to [[Lyon]], where he studied at a [[Society of Jesus|Jesuit]] school for five years. Then, in 1730, he went to [[Paris]] to increase his knowledge of [[mathematics]] and [[physics]]. He made a living by manufacturing [[sundial]]s.

In 1746, he became a member of the [[Académie des Sciences|Academy of Sciences]], and in about 1765 was named ''Censeur Royal''. He was also librarian at the [[University of Strasbourg]], and member of the Academy of Sciences of Paris, Montpellier, Lyon, Amiens, Metz, Berlin, and Stockholm.

==Accomplishments==
[[File:Deparcieux - Essai sur les probabilités, 1746 - 145.tif|thumb|''Essai sur les probabilités'', 1746.]]
Among his constructions were:
* A machine to raise water at [[Crécy-en-Ponthieu|Crécy]] castle
* A pump for castle of [[Arnouville]]
* A press for the production of tobacco

He also published many works, including:
* ''Traité de trigonométrie rectiligne et sphérique'' (1738), approved by the Academy of Sciences
* ''Nouveau traité de trigonométrie, (avec table des sinus et logarithmes)'' (1740)
* ''Traité complet de Gnomonique'' (1741)
* ''Essai sur les probabilités de la durée de la vie humaine'' (1746) ("Essay on the probabilities of the human lifespan"), which is the work for which he is best known<ref>{{Cite Nuttall|title=Deparcieux}}</ref>
* ''Mémoire sur la courbure des ondes'' (1747)

In 1758, Deparcieux was elected a foreign member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]].
